findings.location: .claude/scripts/release-claims-check.sh:88 (sed -n '1,60p') against the header that now runs to :72
findings.evidence: MEASURED, not inferred, and it answers the operator's question (c) with the OPPOSITE of the expected answer: rewriting the header comment DID change behaviour. The R6-F2 fix grew the tally-xref block from 6 lines (:38-43, the span round 6 independently recorded) to 15 (:38-52), pushing everything below it down 9 lines. The help printer is unchanged at `sed -n '1,60p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"` (:88), so the window did not move with the content. `# Exit:` moved from :58 to :67. Measured on the shipped file: `--help` is exactly 60 lines and its last line is `  --ledger   the claims ledger (default: docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md). Also checked` -- cut mid-sentence. grep -c over the rendered help: 'an additional file to check' 0, 'one-line JSON envelope' 0, 'Exit: 0 all surfaces' 0. I reconstructed the pre-round-7 header by splicing round 6's recorded 6-line block back in and re-ran --help on the reconstruction: all three render (1/1/1), with `Exit:` at :58. So the loss is NEW and caused by this round's fix. The range was tuned to the old header -- pre-fix, `1,60p` ended two lines past `Exit:` -- and the header outgrew it. No test asserts the help contract (grep for --help/usage/Exit: in release-claims-check.test.sh returns nothing), so nothing caught it. Everything else is behaviour-neutral: the only two self-referential reads in the file are :76 (PROJECT_DIR via dirname) and :88 (this sed); the TALLY-HISTORY/tally-xref regexes at :163-166 scan surface files, never the script's own source; all five code anchors round 6 cited land at exactly +9 (strip_exempt :146->:155 with the xref `continue` :157->:166, check_table :177->:186, check_tokens :188->:197, check_citations :238->:247, scoping rationale :303->:312), so no code line was added, removed or relocated; bash -n clean; spec 23/23; make lint rc=0.
findings.description: `--help` silently stopped printing the `--surface` semantics ('Missing files are reported and are an error: a surface that silently vanished is how a check stops checking'), the `--json` description, and the entire documented exit contract (0 agree / 1 disagreement / 2 usage-infra), and now ends on a dangling 'Also checked'. NOT HIGH, stated against C9 (accuracy is symmetric -- an overstated defect fails like an understated one): the rendered help asserts nothing FALSE. The omitted material is absent, not contradicted, and no shipped *.md surface documents this tool at all (grep for 'release-claims-check' across every *.md outside docs/reviews/ returns zero hits), so no release claim is falsified. It therefore does not clear the operator's HIGH bar. But it is ALSO not the deferred-INFO class: it makes no true claim more precise -- it is a functional regression introduced by the fix under review, in the same user-facing surface whose verbatim printing is the entire reason R6-F2 was HIGH. Worth naming beside it: the corrected block now ends at :52, eight lines short of the boundary, so eight more header lines added above it would silently drop the R6-F2 fix itself out of --help -- the exact failure mode R6-F2 was raised for. FIX (one token, v5.0.1 or now at the operator's discretion): `sed -n '1,60p'` -> `sed -n '1,67p'` at :88, and ideally an assertion in release-claims-check.test.sh that --help renders the `Exit:` line, so the range cannot silently desynchronise from the header again.
findings.stop_rule_side: neither arm as written: not a false shipped claim (nothing asserted is false), not added precision on a true claim (it is a new functional regression). Non-blocking at risk_threshold=high; the operator decides fix-now vs v5.0.1.
